title: Don't Design a Monster. Design an Ecosystem.
lesson: A creature becomes believable when it has a place in its environment: prey that out-breeds it, a territory, an energy budget, slow breeding, and a job the ecosystem needs it for.

voice.direction: A curious lab-host energy: brisk, warm, a little playful. The hook is a genuine puzzle. 'Press run' is a small grin. The year count is a quick, flat countdown. 'It ends it' lands low and slow. 'The fifth is the twist' teases. Rules one to four are crisp list beats. 'Rule five? Delete the monster' is mischievous; the lesson is sure and warm.

lines.text: If your giant predator eats everything, why hasn't everything gone extinct?
Let's test it. This is the Grimmaw. It eats anything that moves.
Year one: mossbacks everywhere. Year three: thinning. Year five: gone.
With nothing left to hunt, the Grimmaw starves too.
A monster that eats everything doesn't rule your world. It ends it.
Real predators live inside limits. Four are easy. The fifth is the twist.
One: prey that breeds faster than it's eaten.
Two: territory. One Grimmaw needs a whole valley.
Three: energy. A body this big hunts rarely and sleeps a lot.
Four: slow breeding. One cub every few winters.
Now the numbers rise and fall, but nothing vanishes.
The mossbacks boom, strip the meadow bare, then starve.
Rule five is its job. The Grimmaw holds the island together.
Don't design a monster. Design its place in the world.
Share this with someone designing fantasy monsters.

shots.purpose: Stop the scroll on a question with the answer already on screen: a giant predator among its prey.
shots.visual: The Grimmaw in profile on the meadow of the Isle, mossbacks grazing around it; WORLD ENGINE boots top-right as the island ripples.
shots.camera: Long-lens hero shot (fov 16.5 from dist 54, el 8, az 24), slow drift; the last 0.7 s returns to this exact pose.

layers.background: the Isle's peak and the void

shots.lighting: Day mood; warm key from the south-east, hard pixel shadows.
shots.onScreenText: IF IT EATS / EVERYTHING then WHY ISN'T / EVERYTHING / EXTINCT?
shots.music: Hook: the series theme on celesta over strings and a harp sweep; a hit on 'extinct?'.

shots.purpose: Meet the subject and its one dangerous claim, then press RUN.
shots.visual: Field card intro (sprite x3, GRIMMAW, APEX PREDATOR, DIET anything that moves) over the Grimmaw walking in profile; the sim bar slides in and RUN is pressed.
shots.camera: Hero close orbit (az 8), then rise to wide on 'run'.
shots.transition: Ripple + rise to the wide on 'run'.
shots.music: Pulse: pizzicato eighths, the theme's answer on celesta, a soft kick.

shots.purpose: The naive design runs and fails, in numbers.
shots.visual: The whole Isle; clock 0→5, MOSSBACKS 120→0 while the graph falls; herds thin everywhere.
shots.transition: Swoop down to the lone predator.
shots.music: Drive: 16th marimba and quiet square-lead arps, pizzicato, bass, drums.

shots.purpose: Hunger shown as an empty range, never a kill.
shots.visual: The Grimmaw walks an empty meadow at dusk, then lies down and greys. Pin: FOOD IN RANGE / NONE.
shots.music: Drop: cello pedal, a timpani heartbeat, a slowed music-box echo of the theme.

shots.visual: The whole island desaturated and empty; EXTINCT stamp; 'IT ENDS IT.' in rust.
shots.onScreenText: EXTINCT · EVERYTHING · YEAR 5; IT ENDS IT.
shots.music: Near silence; a taiko boom on 'It ends it.'

shots.purpose: Re-hook: rewind the world and open a loop (four easy rules, one locked twist).
shots.visual: REWIND chip and scanlines; clock and herd run back; the checklist card with a blinking locked row 5.
shots.music: Mystery: celesta arpeggios and harp; a reverse-cymbal riser peaks on 'the twist'.

shots.purpose: Rule 1: prey that breeds faster than it is eaten.
shots.visual: Close on a herd; lambs pop in small and grow; pin SPRING +55 BORN; row 1 ticks.
shots.onScreenText: 1 PREY · breeds faster than it's eaten

shots.purpose: Rule 2: territory; the island only fits three.
shots.visual: Top-down Isle; three territory rings painted on the voxels (outside dimmed); two more Grimmaws appear, one per valley; card folds.
shots.onScreenText: 2 RANGE · one valley per Grimmaw; TERRITORY / 1 VALLEY EACH

shots.purpose: Rule 3: a big body hunts rarely and sleeps a lot.
shots.visual: The Grimmaw walks to its den at the foot of the peak and lies down to sleep; Zs.
shots.onScreenText: 3 ENERGY · hunts rarely, sleeps a lot; BIG BODY / HUNTS RARELY

shots.visual: Winter falls over the den (snow on voxels and trees); one cub pops in beside the sleeping Grimmaw.
shots.onScreenText: 4 BREEDING · one cub, every few winters; 1 CUB

shots.purpose: The fixed world runs: it cycles instead of collapsing.
shots.visual: Wide Isle, winters flicker past, years 3→23; graph shows prey and predators rising and falling; STABLE stamp.
shots.music: Drive with the theme on flute and glockenspiel; a stab and cymbal on 'nothing'.

shots.purpose: The locked rule, as an experiment: delete the monster.
shots.visual: RULE 5? then selection brackets + DEL: the three Grimmaws fly apart into voxels; mossbacks boom to 380, strip the meadow to dirt, the forest thins, then the herd crashes.
shots.onScreenText: RULE 5?; DEL; NO PREDATOR graph; MEADOW / STRIPPED BARE
shots.music: A held A7♭9 with a timpani roll, a hard stop on 'Delete', a frenzy for the boom, a chromatic crash into 'starve'.

shots.visual: Row 5 unlocks (ROLE · keeps the grazers in check); the Grimmaws re-appear, the meadow and forest heal, the island ripples on 'together'.
shots.music: Swell: strings and harp rise, a timpani roll into a big D-major hit on 'together'.

shots.purpose: The takeaway: the full design check, screenshot-able.
shots.visual: The complete field card (BEFORE YOU DESIGN A MONSTER / GRIMMAW / 5 rows ticked) with 'Design its place in the world.' in serif italic.
shots.transition: Block wipe to the end card.
shots.music: Anthem: the theme in D major on flute, horns and glockenspiel.

shots.onScreenText: End card; then the hook title.

youtube.description:
If your giant predator eats everything, why hasn't everything gone extinct?

We ran it. The Grimmaw eats anything that moves. By year five the mossbacks are gone, and then the Grimmaw starves too. A monster that eats everything doesn't rule your world. It ends it.

Real predators live inside limits: prey that breeds faster than it's eaten, one territory per predator, a big body that hunts rarely and sleeps a lot, and slow breeding. Then the twist: delete the monster, and the grazers strip the meadow bare and starve instead. The predator was holding the island together.

Don't design a monster. Design its place in the world.
